lesson.title: Pass Where They Aren't
lesson.hook: They're at the net, you have the pass, and you hit it straight onto their racquet.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time they're at the net, look at which side they're covering before you swing, then pass the other one.

pro.label: How the pass is coached
pro.moment: Net players win about two points in three. Craig O'Shannessy teaches the pass by pausing pro footage just before it, to read which side the net player is covering first.
pro.read: Read first, then pass the side they left.

drill.name: The side they left
drill.how: Your partner at the net leans to one side just before you hit. Pass the other side. A pass into the side they covered doesn't count, even if it wins.

steps.name: They cover the line
steps.sit: They approach and close in, shading toward your down-the-line side.
steps.payoff: They covered the line, so the crosscourt was open.
steps.principle: Check which side they're covering before you pick the pass.
steps.why: Shading to the line leaves them too far from the crosscourt ball. The crosscourt also gives you more court and a lower net.
steps.take: They're covering the line? Pass crosscourt.

lines.A: That's the side they're covering: volleyed into your open court.
lines.B: Right onto their racquet: volleyed away.
lines.D: The middle is in their reach: volleyed away.

steps.name: They lean crosscourt
steps.sit: Same approach, but this time they lean over to cover your crosscourt.
steps.payoff: They leaned crosscourt, so the line was open.
steps.principle: The pass goes to the side they've left.
steps.why: Once they commit to one side, they can't get back to the other in time. Change direction and go where they aren't.
steps.take: They're leaning crosscourt? Change direction: down the line.

lines.A: Straight into their lean: volleyed away.
lines.B: They're leaning the other way: passed.
lines.C: Right onto their racquet: volleyed away.
lines.D: Hard, but into their lean: volleyed away.

steps.name: Backhand, they lean crosscourt
steps.sit: Now their approach comes to your backhand. They lean over to cover your crosscourt.
steps.q: Which pass beats them this time?
steps.payoff: Same read on the backhand: they left the line, so pass down it.
steps.principle: Read their position, not which wing you're on.
steps.why: Hard or deep, crosscourt is still the side they're covering. Pace doesn't beat a volleyer who's already there.
steps.take: Either wing: pass the side they left, not the side they cover.

lines.A: Hard, but into their lean: volleyed away.
lines.B: Deep, but into their lean: volleyed away.
lines.C: Right onto their racquet: volleyed away.
lines.D: They left the line open: passed.
